chat.backup.intro: A passphrase you choose locks your keys in a copy that the instance keeps without being able to open it. It is for one thing only: putting the same keys on a new browser, so you get your earlier messages back. It is not a copy of your conversations — those are already on the instance and stay there.
chat.backup.passphrase_hint: If you forget it, it can't be recovered, and the copy becomes useless. The instance never knows it.
chat.backup.restored: Key put back on this browser: you rejoin your conversations, and the history comes back when the other people reopen them.
chat.backup.title: The backup copy
chat.keys.title: The keys to your private messages

chat.mine.title: This device's code
chat.purpose: Here you control who can read your private messages: this device's keys, the copy that brings them elsewhere, and the devices asking to get in.
chat.requests.approved: Approved. From now on it joins your conversations the first time it opens them.
chat.requests.check: Before you say yes, look at the code on that device and check that it is the same one you see here. If it doesn't match, it isn't yours: decline.
chat.requests.declined: Declined: that device has been signed out.

info.about.body: A social network where the content sits physically on a machine that belongs to you, or to your community. There is no algorithm deciding the order, there are no ads, and there is no company in the middle that you have to take at its word.
info.about.local: What you write here is not copied elsewhere. When you delete a post it is really deleted, because no copy of it exists anywhere else.
info.about.title: What ESTIA is
info.connection.title: How you are connected
info.licence.body: ESTIA is free software under the AGPL-3.0. Anyone can read its code, change it and host a copy; whoever offers it to others as a service must make their changes available. It is the licence that makes it hard to turn ESTIA into the very thing it is meant to defend against.
info.licence.title: Licence
keys.how_it_works: The keys to your private messages are created in this browser and stay here: the instance doesn't have them, the people who write to you don't have them, nobody does. That is what makes your messages unreadable even to whoever hosts ESTIA — and it is also why a new browser can't open old messages on its own: another person in the conversation reopens them for it, the first time they reopen that conversation.
keys.many_devices: You can use ESTIA from several devices at once: each one, once approved, joins every conversation by itself the first time you open it, and the others stay on. On a device that has just joined, a conversation's history opens when another person in that conversation reopens it.
keys.missing.next: Open ESTIA from an address that starts with “https://”, or from “localhost” on the machine where the instance runs: the keys are created by themselves, once, and you won't have to do it again.
keys.missing.text: Without them you can't read or write private messages, and — this is the part you don't see — nobody can write to you: anyone who tries is refused. It happens when you sign in from an address the browser doesn't consider secure, because encryption is switched off there.
keys.missing.title: This browser doesn't have the keys for private messages
keys.no_copy.next: Choose a passphrase below and create the copy. It takes ten seconds and you only do it once.
keys.no_copy.text: There is no copy of them. If you sign out here, or if this browser gets cleared, you will come back with a new key: your conversations come back, but this browser stays in them as one more device of yours, and the history reopens only when the other people reopen each conversation.
keys.no_copy.title: The keys are here, but they live only in this browser
keys.sign_out_warning: If you sign out, the key disappears from this browser, and there is no copy of it. When you sign back in, a new one will be created: you will find your conversations again, but the history will reopen only when the other people reopen them, and this browser will stay in them as one more device of yours.
keys.waiting.next: Open ESTIA on a device where you are already signed in, go to Settings → Chat, and compare the code you see there with the one below. If they match, say yes.
keys.waiting.text: The keys are here, but nobody has said yet that this device is you. While it waits it doesn't join your conversations, and nothing changes on the device you already had — nothing gets lost.
keys.waiting.title: This device is waiting for your yes
keys.with_copy.text: There is a copy on the instance, updated on {{date}}. When you sign in from a new browser you can put this same key back with your passphrase, and rejoin your conversations in place of the old browser.
keys.with_copy.title: The keys are here, and you have a copy

presence.instance.public_note: Whoever opens your profile sees your posts. They can follow you without waiting for a yes.
presence.network.intro: On the network between instances, if you are in EstiaNet, anyone can find you when searching linked instances. Here you decide what people see when they open your profile: your posts, or only the option to ask to follow you.
presence.network.intro_outside: On the network between instances, if you are in EstiaNet, anyone can find you when searching linked instances. Here you decide what people see when they open your profile: your posts, or only the option to ask to follow you. It applies once you join EstiaNet: while you are outside, it is only a preference.

presence.private_note: Whoever opens your profile can ask to follow you. They see your posts only after you accept.
